saga.title: აღმაშენებლის ხანა — The Age of David the Builder

beats.narration: On the eve of Didgori, the twelfth of August, 1121, King დავით აღმაშენებელი kneels in prayer while a vast Seljuk coalition fills the plain below. He is outnumbered many times over. Witness a king who built churches and academies now stake the recovered life of his nation on a single morning.

David has remade his army from a scattered, broken thing into one disciplined host — Georgians, and allies, bound to a single will. Aid the muster: carry the word along the lines, close the ranks for the narrow valley where numbers will not save the enemy.

The Aspect of the Invading Tide breaks against the Georgian line — the erasing pressure of a century of raids, that would leave Kartli a road for armies and nothing of its own. This is the great defensive stand, the meaning of Ward. Hold the line at Didgori until the Tide breaks upon it.

The host is broken and the day is won — ძლევაჲ საკვირველი, the wondrous victory, that the chroniclers could explain only as a gift from God. Witness the morning a nation that had nearly been erased stood up whole on the field.

The next year David takes Tbilisi back after four centuries and makes it again the capital — and enters it as a builder, not a destroyer. Restore the city to the crown and the crown to its memory. The Builder's name will mean exactly this: not conquest, but a homeland set back upon its foundations.

David lays his own grave at the gate of Gelati, to be trodden by all who pass — a king who would be humble even in stone. The Golden Age opens before his people. You have kept it; the thread blazes in the Living Chronicle. The way to the apex is open.
